title: Aristotle Physics II.8 regular-purpose versus incidental-result constructor
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED. Physics II.8 gives a complete causal content system distinguishing a regular natural series toward an end from an incidental result, with material necessity, impediment and agent-capacity conditions retained. The same broad rain/result chain changes relation without changing names.

source.source_span: chapter 8: rain/crop objection, teeth challenge, regularity rebuttal, natural means/end examples, failure and impediment qualifications
source.source_limit: public English translation; no claim about a target language, medieval witness, or modern natural law

steps: REGISTER natural series, candidate end, material chain and result
CLASSIFY result as regular/usual or incidental and record impediment
IF regular and unimpeded, emit FOR_END(series,end)
IF end-like result is incidental, emit INCIDENTAL(result,cause); use CHANCE only when the source's deliberating-agent condition is met, otherwise SPONTANEOUS
IF a purposive sequence fails, emit FAILED_ATTEMPT(series,intended_end) while retaining the intended end
Keep material conditions as ENABLES(material,product), not automatically as final cause

consequence: Ordinary regular rain-to-crop growth can receive FOR_END while a one-off spoiled crop remains INCIDENTAL under the same broad event family. A result-is-purpose rival cannot preserve both source cases; an all-chance rival loses regularity.
rival: R-II8-result-purpose: every observed result is treated as the event's purpose; alternate R-II8-all-chance marks every natural sequence incidental.
symmetries: equivalent paraphrase of typed cause labels
missing_target_binding: No target word is assigned to purpose, chance, nature, material, regularity, or impediment. A future writer must expose all these arguments globally; no generic connector is credited.
likely_failure: Without independently bound regularity, impediment and cause-kind fields, the constructor degenerates into arbitrary post-hoc labels and has no discriminating force.
